commit.message:
fix(bash): pass per-exec env to nested sh/bash and stop leaking parent vars (#439)

* fix(bash): pass per-exec env to nested sh/bash and stop leaking parent vars

`Bash.exec(..., { env, replaceEnv: true })` put the per-exec variables in
the environment map but never marked them exported, and nested `sh`/`bash`
merged its exported env onto the persistent shell instead of replacing it.
A nested shell therefore missed the per-exec variables while still seeing
the constructor's env, and unexported variables leaked into children.

- Bash.exec marks per-exec env keys as exported (valid names only, so the
  positional parameters nested shells pass through env stay local); with
  replaceEnv it starts from an empty export set. The set is copied per exec
  so an `export` in one exec no longer leaks into later ones.
- replaceEnv keeps the shell-maintained SHELLOPTS and BASHOPTS.
- Nested sh/bash runs with replaceEnv, starting from the exported env plus
  what a new shell sets up itself: a default PATH, host variables
  (OSTYPE, HOSTNAME, ...) and IFS/OPTIND, which bash never imports.

Fixes #438

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(bash): initialize nested-shell variables unexported, stop env/time leak

Address review on #439:

- Only the host `Bash.exec` API and new shells treat `env` as the
  environment and export its keys. Internal callers such as `env` and
  `time` pass the full variable map, so exporting it re-leaked unexported
  variables (`FOO=secret; env sh -c 'echo $FOO'`).
- Nested sh/bash now asks for a new shell (`newShell`) instead of seeding
  variables through `env`. Bash.exec initializes PATH, OSTYPE, HOSTNAME,
  ... from fixed defaults when the environment lacks them, and always
  resets IFS, OPTIND, SHELLOPTS and BASHOPTS, all unexported. Unexported
  parent values (`HOSTNAME=secret; export -n HOSTNAME`) no longer reach
  the child, and `export -p` there no longer lists them.
- SHELLOPTS/BASHOPTS are no longer injected into a host `replaceEnv`
  exec, so `env -i printenv` stays empty of them.
- `replaceEnv` no longer falls back to the parent's previous directory,
  so `cd -` in a child without OLDPWD reports "OLDPWD not set".
- Drop the banned `|| {}` fallback and add a changeset.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(bash): inherit the caller's env and exports in recursive exec

Address review on #439: recursive execution (from `env`, `time`,
`timeout`, ...) started from the instance's persistent state. Copying its
export set, as the previous commit did, dropped exports made earlier in
the running script, so `export FOO=bar; env sh -c 'echo $FOO'` lost FOO.
Starting from its env let a `replaceEnv` exec get the constructor env back
through `timeout 5 printenv SECRET`.

The interpreter's exec callback now hands over the calling execution's
live state. A recursive exec starts from that state's variables and its
export set, including prefix exports (`FOO=x timeout 5 sh -c ...`), still
copied so nothing leaks back.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(bash): preserve startup exports and use live OLDPWD

* test(bash): exercise time wrapper and explicit cd startup state

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: Hiroki Osame <hiroki.osame@gmail.com>

commit.message:
fix(bash): write the /bin and /usr/bin command stubs as executable

Bash.registerCommand wrote every /bin/<name> and /usr/bin/<name> stub
with writeFileSync(path, stub) and no mode, so InMemoryFs and OverlayFs
stored DEFAULT_FILE_MODE (0o644). The -x file test checks mode & 0o100,
so `test -x /usr/bin/ls` returned 1 and `stat -c %a /usr/bin/ls` printed
644 although /usr/bin/ls runs. autoconf's as_fn_executable_p
(`test -f $f && test -x $f`) rejected every built-in command, so a
configure script stopped with "no acceptable grep could be found".

I pass { mode: 0o755 } as the stub metadata. InMemoryFs.writeFileSync
already takes that optional 4th argument. I add the same optional
arguments to OverlayFs.writeFileSync (stores metadata.mode and
metadata.mtime) and to MountableFs.writeFileSync (forwards options and
metadata to the owning filesystem). Both changes are backwards
compatible. DEFAULT_FILE_MODE, the -x test and ls stay unchanged.

The new test src/command-stubs.executable.test.ts covers test -x,
[ -x ], stat -c %a, an IFS=: PATH probe, OverlayFs and MountableFs.

Before the fix (upstream main 58d1ecf)

    $ pnpm --filter just-bash exec vitest run src/command-stubs.executable.test.ts
     FAIL  ... are executable for test -x, [ -x ] and stat
    AssertionError: expected 'usr=1\nbin=1\n644\n' to be 'usr=0\nbin=0\n755\n'
     FAIL  ... are found by an autoconf-style PATH probe
    AssertionError: expected '' to be '/usr/bin/grep\n'
     FAIL  ... are executable on OverlayFs
    AssertionError: expected '1\n' to be '0\n'
     FAIL  ... are executable on MountableFs
    AssertionError: expected '1\n' to be '0\n'
          Tests  4 failed (4)

After the fix

    $ pnpm --filter just-bash exec vitest run src/command-stubs.executable.test.ts
     Test Files  1 passed (1)
          Tests  4 passed (4)

End to end with new Bash().exec() through tsx against src/index.ts

    $ test -x /usr/bin/ls; echo test=$?; [ -x /bin/cat ]; echo bracket=$?; stat -c %a /usr/bin/ls /bin/grep
    before: test=1 bracket=1 644 644
    after:  test=0 bracket=0 755 755
    $ dirs=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin; IFS=:; for d in $dirs; do f="$d/grep"; if test -f "$f" && test -x "$f"; then echo found=$f; break; fi; done
    before: (no output)
    after:  found=/usr/bin/grep
    $ /usr/bin/echo hi; command -v grep; type -P ls
    before and after: hi /usr/bin/grep /usr/bin/ls
    $ printf 'echo user\n' > /tmp/u.sh; /tmp/u.sh; echo rc=$?
    before and after: rc=126 (Permission denied, a 644 user script stays non-executable)

Wider checks

    $ pnpm --filter just-bash typecheck
    rc=0
    $ pnpm lint
    rc=0 (biome checked 1203 files, no fixes; no banned patterns)
    $ pnpm --filter just-bash test:unit
    branch: Tests 85 failed | 15054 passed | 100 skipped (15239)
    main:   Tests 85 failed | 15050 passed | 100 skipped (15235)
    The 85 failing tests are the same list on main and on the branch
    (bundle, dist, CLI, tar.bundle, read-write-fs mode, security dist checks).

Not run are pnpm test:dist and the autoconf 2.73 configure end to end,
because this environment has no built dist and no configure script.

@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+---
+"just-bash": patch
+---
+
+Write the `/bin` and `/usr/bin` command stubs with mode 755, so `test -x`, `stat` and PATH probes such as autoconf's `as_fn_executable_p` see them as executable. `OverlayFs.writeFileSync` and `MountableFs.writeFileSync` accept the optional `metadata` argument that `InMemoryFs.writeFileSync` already takes.
